children: Tyson Foods said its revenue will grow by less than previously expected this year, citing pressure on volatile cattle prices.
The company said Thursday that it expects revenue in fiscal 2026 to rise by 1.5% to 2%, down from a previous range of 2.5% to 3.5%.
Shares fell 7.4% to $51.68 in Thursday morning trading. The stock is down 12% this year.

"The revised outlook is primarily driven by significant margin compression amid volatile cattle prices and one of the most severe cattle shortages in U.S. history, as well as the expected impact of lower cattle prices on the value of live cattle inventories," the company said Thursday.
Beef producers have been grappling with a yearslong cattle shortage and posting substantial losses, even as consumer prices for beef remain high, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Tyson said its beef segment is now expected to generate an adjusted operating loss of $625 million to $775 million for the fiscal year. It previously guided for a loss between $500 million and $650 million.

Tyson also cut guidance for adjusted operating profits for its other meat segments. It said the chicken segment is expected to turn a profit between $1.85 billion and $1.95 billion, below previous guidance for $1.9 billion to $2.05 billion, due to consumer caution.

Softer hog and wholesale pricing means the pork segment is now expected to generate an adjusted operating profit of between $200 million and $250 million, the company said, down $50 million from Tyson's prior outlook.

The move follows Tyson announcing plans last month to shutter one beef processing plant and sell another as part of a pullback from the beef business. The company's beef restructuring should reduce operating cost pressures in fiscal 2027, Chief Executive Donnie King said Thursday.
